 Dortmund vs Elversberg Predicted Lineup: Silva Starts
 Dortmund's predicted lineup against Elversberg on Saturday 7 November: Silva leads the line in a 3-4-2-1 with Guirassy injured, Karetsas and Beier behind him.
 TB Tunde Bakare 
 Thu 5 Nov 2026, 14:47 GMT 4 min read 
 Updated 17:12, 5 Nov GMT Comment 
 Borussia Dortmund 
 Signal Iduna Park under floodlights. Photo by Waldemar Brandt on Unsplash (Unsplash License). 
 Borussia Dortmund host Elversberg at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday 7 November in Bundesliga matchday 9 , with Fabio Silva in line to lead the line in a 3-4-2-1 after Serhou Guirassy went off injured in Wednesday’s 2-1 Champions League win over Real Betis. Niko Kovac’s side are unbeaten in the league and level on 18 points with Bayern Munich, who sit top on goal difference. 
 In this article 
 The match and the stakes 
 Team news 
 The predicted XI 
 How Dortmund will play 
 The lineup in full 
 The match and the stakes
 Dortmund have taken 18 points from eight league games and haven’t lost in the Bundesliga this season. Bayern are on the same total after the 2-2 draw between the two sides in Munich on Saturday 31 October, a game in which Dortmund twice came from behind and set a club record by covering 127.6 kilometres.
 Elversberg aren’t a routine home fixture. The newcomers sit seventh with 13 points from eight games and four wins, the latest a 4-1 win over Mainz, and around 8,000 of their supporters are expected at Signal Iduna Park. This is the first league meeting between the clubs. Their only previous competitive game was a DFB Cup tie in October 1981, which Dortmund won 4-1.
 Wednesday’s win over Betis took Dortmund to nine Champions League points, and the league schedule now gives them a home game they are expected to win before the international break. Dropping points here would hand Bayern the chance to open a gap at the top without playing Dortmund again until the return fixture.
 Team news
 Guirassy is the main absence. He went off injured in the 31st minute against Betis and was replaced by Konstantinos Karetsas, and the expectation is that he misses this game. Silva, who scored the opener on 49 minutes and set up the winner, is the natural replacement as the central striker. That change, and what Silva does differently in the role, is covered in our tactical analysis of the Betis win .
 Karetsas scored that winner in the 72nd minute, five minutes after Aitor Ruibal had equalised for Betis following an error by Waldemar Anton. A start for the teenager behind Silva is the other change we expect, with Carney Chukwuemeka dropping to the bench.
 The longer-term list is unchanged. Emre Can has been doing individual training, Konstantelias has a torn ACL and Lerma has had muscle issues. None of the three was in the squad at Bayern, and there’s no indication any of them returns this weekend.
 The predicted XI
 Borussia Dortmund predicted XI (3-4-2-1)
 Silva 
 Karetsas 
 Beier 
 Svensson 
 Bellingham 
 Veerman 
 Ryerson 
 Bensebaini 
 Schlotterbeck 
 Anton 
 Kobel 
 Gregor Kobel keeps his place in goal. The back three stays as it was: Anton on the right, captain Nico Schlotterbeck in the middle and Ramy Bensebaini on the left. Bensebaini is the left-footed passer in that line, which matters when teams press Dortmund’s first pass out of defence.
 Read next Bayern Munich Karl at No 10, Brown on the Left: Danks’ Bayern Lineup at Mainz 
 Julian Ryerson and Daniel Svensson are the wing-backs, with Jobe Bellingham and Joey Veerman in the middle. Felix Nmecha and Marcel Sabitzer are the options if Kovac wants fresh legs in that pair after a Champions League midweek.
 Ahead of them, Karetsas and Maximilian Beier play behind Silva. Beier keeps his place in that line, and Karetsas joins him after deciding the Betis game from the bench.
 How Dortmund will play
 The back three is a build-up choice. Against a first line of pressure, Dortmund have a spare man at the back, and Schlotterbeck can step into midfield with the ball rather than playing the safe pass wide. That mechanism is the base of the defensive structure Kovac has built this season , and it’s why Dortmund can control home games against sides who sit in.
 The risk is the space behind the wing-backs. When Ryerson and Svensson both push high, Anton and Bensebaini have to defend the channels, and Anton’s error against Betis came when he was pulled into exactly that kind of moment. Elversberg’s clearest route is the same one: win the ball, then play into the space a wing-back has left, with Cole Campbell, who joined Elversberg from Dortmund this summer and scored late in the 4-1 win over Mainz, running that channel.
 Guirassy plays on the last line and waits for service. Silva drops off the front, links the play and then arrives in the box, which is how he scored against Betis, following in Jobe Bellingham’s parried shot. With Karetsas and Beier starting closer to him than wingers would, Dortmund should get numbers around the second balls rather than leaving the striker to chase clearances, the same front line shape we set out for the Betis game with a different name at the top of it.
 The lineup in full
 Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel; Anton, Schlotterbeck, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Bellingham, Veerman, Svensson; Karetsas, Beier; Silva.
 Kick-off at Signal Iduna Park is at 15:30 CET on Saturday. Dortmund’s next game after the international break is away to Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday 21 November.
